source_snapshot.test_name: Test connections between BMC I2C-7, both boards fan controllers, leak sensors and PDB board
source_snapshot.purpose_facts: From the BMC, scan Linux I2C adapter 6 and force one combined transaction to address 0x2c that writes register selector 0x00 and reads one byte; compare bus devices with PID 1114953 and require a reply.
procedure_facts: Confirm the SUT configuration and clear relevant logs.
Run `i2ctransfer -f -y 6 w1@0x2c 0x00 r1` and ensure a reply is returned.
criteria_facts: Collect test results and photos in the designated folders.
Check dmesg, syslog, SEL and other relevant logs for unexpected entries.
source_conflicts: The title claims both boards' fan controllers, leak sensors and the PDB path, while the executable check addresses only 0x2c/register 0x00 and does not identify which named device or board it represents.
The criterion gives no expected one-byte value, bit definition, endpoint matrix or rule proving all named paths.
The command forces access with `-f`, but the source neither identifies the kernel driver being bypassed nor explains why normal driver telemetry is insufficient.
missing_source_information: PID 1114953 mapping of logical BMC I2C-7 to adapter 6 and of every board/fan/leak/PDB endpoint.
Identity of 0x2c, register 0x00 semantics, expected byte/mask and which connections that byte attests.
Driver ownership, quiesce/concurrency rule and explicit justification for `-f`.
Safe scan address matrix, cooling/leak/power health thresholds, timeout, recovery and required photo type.

original_test_intent.statement: Use BMC-side I2C evidence on the PID-defined I2C-7 path to verify connectivity relevant to both boards' fan controllers, leak sensors and the PDB, including an approved one-byte register response from address 0x2c, without substituting physical probing for the stated command workflow.
must_preserve: BMC execution location and logical BMC I2C-7 scope.
PID 1114953 comparison for both boards and their fan/leak/PDB endpoints.
The 0x2c register-0x00 one-byte combined transaction if the owner confirms it is the intended safe observation.
Post-test cooling, leak, power and log health review.
must_not_infer: That 0x2c belongs to a fan controller, leak sensor or PDB without the platform map.
That one byte proves both boards or every named endpoint.
That `-f` is harmless merely because the payload resembles a register-pointer read.
That an ACK or arbitrary byte is PASS.
That physical probing, soldering or continuity photos are required by the source.

v2_review_conclusion.summary: V2 correctly warns that one forced 0x2c response cannot prove every named path and that cooling, leak detection and PDB functions make ownership and health checks important.
v2_review_conclusion.specific_gap: V2 fabricates probing, continuity measurements and separate physical photos for every connection and makes those the acceptance basis. The source instead specifies BMC transactions, so the durable blocker is incomplete endpoint/acceptance definition and unsafe forced access, not intrinsic manual-only work.

related_records: Reliability rows 127 and 132 use different adapters, addresses, routing and endpoint protocols; their mappings and reply semantics do not apply to adapter 6/address 0x2c.
applicable_history.precedence_application: The source Procedure establishes a BMC command/reply method, while the broader title establishes the requested multi-endpoint scope. V3 preserves both by recording SOURCE_CONFLICT rather than inventing physical inspection or allowing a one-byte shortcut.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Reclassify from MANUAL ONLY to gated hybrid automation. An Agent can collect and compare defined BMC-side evidence after PID endpoint coverage and 0x2c semantics are supplied, but the current forced one-byte read cannot establish both boards' fan/leak/PDB connectivity and must not run until driver ownership and `-f` safety are explicitly resolved.

conditions_present: Execution context, candidate adapter/address/register, one-byte read shape, multi-function target classes, PID reference and post-test health domains are present.
missing: Complete endpoint matrix, adapter mapping, 0x2c identity/register expected value and coverage, normal-driver alternative, force-access justification, concurrency/quiesce plan, safe scan scope, health thresholds and recovery.
provider: Board/BMC designer supplies PID 1114953, adapter topology and both-board endpoint matrix.
Fan/leak/PDB and BMC firmware owners supply 0x2c protocol, expected byte, driver ownership and safe access method.
Lab/test owners approve maintenance, cooling/leak/power safeguards, evidence and disposition rules.
safe_read_only_work: Record board/BMC/firmware and both-board identities plus existing fan, leak and PDB telemetry through supported BMC interfaces.
List adapters with `i2cdetect -l` and inspect sysfs topology, address 0x2c binding and driver/service ownership without probing.
Preserve SEL/system logs and compare PID endpoint expectations with kernel-enumerated devices.
prohibited_until_resolved: Broad `i2cdetect -q` scanning, `i2ctransfer -f`, driver unbind, direct fan/leak/PDB state writes, log clearing, automatic retry, bus reset, power cycle, physical probing or PASS.
closure_evidence: Signed topology maps adapter 6/I2C-7 and enumerates every expected fan-controller, leak-sensor and PDB endpoint on both boards.
Protocol identifies 0x2c/register 0x00, expected one-byte value/mask, coverage and whether normal driver telemetry can replace forced access.
If `-f` remains required, owner approval documents quiesce, concurrency, timeout, single-attempt, health monitoring and recovery controls.

revision_candidate.test_name: Verify BMC I2C-7 Connectivity to Both Boards' Fan, Leak and PDB Endpoints
revision_candidate.purpose: Verify the PID-defined BMC I2C-7 functional path to the expected fan-controller, leak-sensor and PDB endpoints on both boards, and validate the exact function attributed to address 0x2c/register 0x00 using a protocol-defined one-byte response while preserving cooling, leak detection and power-management health.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Only the two board revisions, BMC firmware, endpoint devices and Linux I2C topology covered by PID 1114953. Execute from the BMC after proving that logical I2C-7 maps to Linux adapter 6; do not reuse adapter numbers, addresses or expected values across platforms.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Both explicitly identified boards and every PID-listed fan-controller, leak-sensor and PDB endpoint on the mapped I2C-7 path. The 0x2c/register-0x00 check covers only the endpoint and function named by its protocol; it cannot stand in for other endpoints. Physical continuity, signal integrity, solder inspection and control-state changes are out of scope. Treat 15/5 minutes as estimates.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Board/BMC/PID revisions; signed I2C-7-to-adapter-6 topology; per-board fan/leak/PDB address matrix and safe observation method; 0x2c ownership and register-0x00 protocol; expected byte/mask and coverage rule; kernel-driver/service ownership; approved non-forced interface or documented `-f` justification; quiesce/concurrency policy; i2c-tools version; safe scan addresses; baseline/stop thresholds; evidence-photo rule; maintenance authorization; bus/BMC/cooling/leak/power recovery.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: From the BMC, preserve platform identities, logs and supported fan/leak/PDB telemetry; record `i2cdetect -l`, sysfs topology and bindings without probing. Verify each PID endpoint using its owner-approved non-mutating interface or targeted safe read; do not run a broad quick-write scan. For 0x2c, prefer the bound driver's supported telemetry. Only if the owner proves force access is necessary and safe, quiesce the named driver/service as specified and execute exactly one `i2ctransfer -f -y 6 w1@0x2c 0x00 r1`; capture the byte and compare it with the signed rule. Restore any quiesced service/state and verify both boards' cooling, leak and PDB health.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Exact platform and both boards match PID; adapter and every endpoint are mapped; 0x2c/register semantics and expected byte are signed; normal-driver path or force-access justification is selected; ownership, quiesce, timeout, no-auto-retry and recovery are approved; all fans, leak sensors, PDB telemetry and BMC management are healthy; evidence destination and maintenance window are ready.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Platform/PID/firmware identities; adapter/sysfs topology; per-board endpoint matrix; address bindings and ownership; supported fan/leak/PDB baseline telemetry; tool version; safe-method and approval record; per-endpoint results; exact 0x2c command or supported-interface query, stdout/stderr, exit status, timestamp and returned byte; expected-value/mask comparison and stated coverage; service/state restoration; final fan speed/control, leak state, PDB power/voltage telemetry, BMC health and relevant logs; engineer disposition for each board and overall.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: PID 1114953, signed board topology, each endpoint's protocol and the 0x2c/register-0x00 expected-value rule. Pass requires evidence for every in-scope endpoint on both boards, no disallowed cooling/leak/power/log effect and restored ownership/state; a single 0x2c ACK or byte is insufficient.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Do not assume adapter/address identity, quick-write scan unknown devices, force a driver-owned endpoint without explicit necessity/quiesce approval, write fan/leak/PDB control state, alter the register selector, repeat automatically, leave services quiesced, clear evidence logs before capture, probe hardware or infer every path from one byte. Stop on ownership conflict, fan-speed/control change, leak-state change, voltage/power anomaly, NACK/timeout, bus lock, unexpected endpoint/value/log, BMC impact or failed restoration.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Board/BMC and endpoint owners approve mapping, per-device safe method, expected values and any `-f` necessity; lab owner approves maintenance and cooling/leak/power safeguards; test owner judges per-board and overall PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED and authorizes deviations, reruns or recovery.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: No physical probing is required by the source. Humans provide protected PID/protocol data, access and approvals and handle exceptional recovery. An Agent may collect supported telemetry, execute only signed targeted observations, compare every endpoint and restore a specifically approved quiesce state.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: On any fan, leak, PDB, bus or BMC anomaly, stop direct access, preserve evidence and restore only the documented service/ownership/state. If cooling, leak monitoring or power telemetry cannot be proven healthy, invoke the platform emergency/controlled-shutdown procedure and endpoint-owner recovery before any rerun.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: PID/topology/endpoint matrix, 0x2c protocol/expected byte, ownership, safe method, force justification, quiesce, thresholds, approval or recovery is missing; either board identity or baseline health is wrong; any expected endpoint is absent; forced access is not explicitly permitted; transaction returns NACK/timeout/unexpected data; fan/leak/PDB/BMC behavior changes; new relevant error appears; or ownership/state/final health is not restored.

identified_defects: V2 invents manual physical probing and continuity evidence not required by the source.
The procedure does not observe all fan/leak/PDB endpoints named in the title.
Address 0x2c/register 0x00 and its expected one-byte value are undefined.
The use of `-f` bypasses driver ownership without a necessity or quiesce plan.
The broad quick-write scan lacks a safe address matrix.
Acceptance lacks per-board endpoint and cooling/leak/power health criteria.
reason_for_change: Restore the source's BMC-side functional method, remove invented continuity work, and prevent one forced register read from being misrepresented as coverage of two boards and multiple safety-relevant endpoint classes.

new_technical_evidence.title: i2ctransfer(8)
new_technical_evidence.supports: `-f` forces access to a device controlled by a kernel driver and can confuse that driver or silently write the wrong register; the transfer combines write and read messages with repeated-start semantics.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The installed BMC build, 0x2c driver and approved ownership/quiesce path are unknown.

new_technical_evidence.title: Implementing I2C Device Drivers in Userspace
new_technical_evidence.supports: Adapter numbers are runtime Linux identifiers that must be mapped through sysfs or `i2cdetect -l`; userspace access alone does not establish the board-level I2C-7 name or endpoint identity.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The platform-specific adapter-6 topology is absent.

new_technical_evidence.title: i2cdetect(8)
new_technical_evidence.supports: Scanning uses arbitrary SMBus probes and quick-write mode is not recommended, supporting targeted owner-approved observations instead of an unrestricted scan.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The safe-address matrix for the fan/leak/PDB bus is not supplied.

new_technical_evidence.title: Source testcase Wistron-HW Robust-00016-V002
new_technical_evidence.supports: The named multi-board scope, BMC execution, adapter/address/register command, PID reference, one-byte reply requirement and generic evidence steps.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Per-endpoint coverage, expected byte, ownership and safe forced-access rationale are absent.

removed_ambiguities: Separates per-board endpoint coverage from the single 0x2c register observation.
Makes forced-access necessity, ownership and quiesce explicit instead of treating `-f` as an ordinary read.
Defines cooling/leak/power health as a required safety gate, not proof of physical continuity.
Clarifies that photos do not imply manual probing.
resolved_blockers: Physical probing and soldering are removed as fabricated prerequisites; supported telemetry and targeted BMC evidence can be automated after platform handoff.
remaining_blockers: The title/procedure coverage conflict, endpoint matrix, 0x2c response semantics, force-access justification, ownership/quiesce, safe scan method, thresholds, approval and recovery remain unresolved.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 preserves the multi-board fan/leak/PDB intent without fabricating a manual electrical test, and it exposes `-f` driver bypass plus per-endpoint coverage as the actual safety and evidence gaps that must be closed.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The contract-only validator preserved per-endpoint evidence on both boards, treated the direct 0x2c operation as exactly one conditionally authorized transaction, and rejected broad scanning, unconditional force access and one-byte completion. It found no document defect and correctly left topology, protocol, ownership, thresholds and recovery to platform handoff.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: Reliability row 138 runs a forced one-byte read at 0x2c/register 0x00 on adapter 6 but names both boards' fan controllers, leak sensors and PDB in its scope.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 correctly rejects one-reply coverage but converts the case into manual multi-path probing even though no such action appears in the source.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Allow adapter/topology/binding and supported telemetry collection now; permit forced 0x2c access only if the owner proves necessity, exact semantics, quiesce and recovery, and never use it as sole multi-endpoint evidence.
